concepts.definition: A broad fallback for a directly perceived alteration in vision whose specific form cannot be determined from the report; it is not a label for generic strangeness.
concepts.name: visual distortions

concepts.definition: Organized, repeated, or decorative motifs become unusually prominent in or across the visual field, without requiring explicitly geometric or self-similar structure.
concepts.name: patterning

concepts.definition: Fine visual texture appears to travel in small wave-like undulations across a surface, rather than the whole surface rhythmically expanding as in surface breathing.
concepts.name: texture rippling

concepts.definition: A surface appears to swell and contract in a slow, coherent rhythm resembling breathing, distinct from directional drifting or fluid-like visual liquefaction.
concepts.name: surface breathing

concepts.definition: Objects or surfaces appear to melt, flow, drip, or behave as a continuous fluid while remaining visual experiences rather than beliefs about physical transformation.
concepts.name: visual liquefaction

concepts.definition: Objects, surfaces, faces, text, or parts of the visual field appear bent, stretched, twisted, or otherwise deformed without continuously changing identity.
concepts.name: warping

concepts.definition: Objects, faces, patterns, or visual forms appear to transform continuously into other shapes, identities, structures, or forms rather than merely bending in place.
concepts.name: morphing

concepts.definition: Stationary objects, patterns, surfaces, or portions of the visual field appear to slide, float, sway, or slowly move from their expected position.
concepts.name: drifting

concepts.definition: Surfaces, edges, textures, light, or the visual field appear to flicker, glint, ripple with light, or show an unsteady luminous instability.
concepts.name: shimmering

concepts.definition: Objects, edges, patterns, or the visual field appear to tremble, oscillate, buzz, or rapidly quiver in place without undergoing a larger displacement.
concepts.name: visual vibration

concepts.definition: Self-similar visual forms repeat at multiple apparent scales, often branching or unfolding into recursively detailed structure rather than simple repeated motifs.
concepts.name: fractal imagery

concepts.definition: Grids, lattices, tessellations, mandala-like forms, angular structures, or other abstract geometric patterns are seen; their color and eye state belong in detail.
concepts.name: geometric imagery

concepts.definition: Internally generated image-like content is experienced and recognized as imagery, with its eye state and subject matter recorded as detail rather than separate effects.
concepts.name: visual imagery

concepts.definition: Unformed light, color, flashes, points, lines, or elementary shapes are perceived without an ordinary external source and as present in perceptual space.
concepts.name: simple visual hallucination

concepts.definition: Fully formed objects, people, animals, entities, or scenes are perceived without an ordinary external source; the depicted content belongs in detail.
concepts.name: complex visual hallucination

concepts.definition: Successive residual copies appear behind a moving object or viewpoint, tracing its recent path rather than leaving one stationary image after the object disappears.
concepts.name: visual trails

concepts.definition: A visual impression persists or recurs after the original stimulus has moved or vanished, distinct from a chain of copies continuously following motion.
concepts.name: afterimages

concepts.definition: Real movement appears unusually large, fast, forceful, or visually emphasized even though its direction and continuity remain recognizable.
concepts.name: motion exaggeration

concepts.definition: Colors appear unusually vivid, pure, or intense in chromatic strength, distinct from a general increase in luminance or contrast.
concepts.name: color saturation enhancement

concepts.definition: The visual field, lights, or objects appear more luminous or brightly lit than expected, without necessarily becoming more colorful or sharply contrasted.
concepts.name: brightness enhancement

concepts.definition: Differences between light and dark, colors, edges, or adjacent regions appear unusually pronounced, producing stronger visual separation.
concepts.name: contrast enhancement

concepts.definition: Edges and fine spatial detail appear unusually crisp or resolvable, distinct from merely brighter, more saturated, or more meaningful vision.
concepts.name: visual acuity enhancement

concepts.definition: Numerous fine, rapidly changing dots resembling television static are seen across a substantial portion of the visual field.
concepts.name: visual snow

concepts.definition: Existing visual regularities and organized forms are detected more readily than usual, without necessarily misidentifying ambiguous material as a specific object.
concepts.name: pattern recognition enhancement

concepts.definition: Ambiguous real visual material is perceived as a meaningful familiar form, such as a face or figure, rather than a formed image appearing without a stimulus.
concepts.name: pareidolia

concepts.definition: Objects, body parts, people, or environmental features appear unusually enlarged, reduced, inflated, or shrunken relative to their expected size.
concepts.name: size distortion

concepts.definition: Objects, people, or environmental features appear closer or farther away than their expected location, while their perceived size may remain independently unchanged.
concepts.name: distance distortion

concepts.definition: The depth structure of a scene changes so that space appears flattened, layered, recessed, expanded, or otherwise altered in three-dimensional organization.
concepts.name: depth distortion

concepts.definition: Body parts, objects, or spatial forms appear unnaturally compressed or elongated along the viewer's line of sight.
concepts.name: foreshortening distortion

concepts.definition: A scene's geometric relations appear skewed: angles, proportions, orientation, convergence, or lines of sight no longer fit the expected viewpoint.
concepts.name: perspective distortion

concepts.definition: Part or all of the visible scene appears replaced by a different place, setting, or constructed environment rather than merely altered in style.
concepts.name: scene replacement

concepts.definition: The existing environment remains recognizable yet appears transformed in character, style, material, atmosphere, or identity.
concepts.name: environmental transfiguration

concepts.definition: The visual scene or an attended region appears to enlarge or recede as though a camera lens were zooming, without ordinary movement toward or away from it.
concepts.name: zooming

concepts.definition: Objects or the scene appear divided into separate slices, tiles, shards, or discontinuous parts instead of one spatially coherent image.
concepts.name: visual fragmentation

concepts.definition: One object or image appears as two or more simultaneous copies; the number of copies and binocular or monocular context belong in detail.
concepts.name: visual multiplicity

concepts.definition: Visual boundaries and fine details lose focus and spread into one another, resembling an out-of-focus image rather than a fog laid over the scene.
concepts.name: blurred vision

concepts.definition: The usable or attended visual field appears constricted toward its center, with peripheral vision diminished or absent.
concepts.name: field narrowing

concepts.definition: The visual field appears unusually broad or panoramic, with more peripheral extent or awareness than is ordinarily experienced.
concepts.name: field widening

concepts.definition: Luminous rings, glows, coronas, or radiating haze appear around lights or bright objects rather than uniformly across the whole scene.
concepts.name: light haloing

concepts.definition: A color cast overlays objects or the visual field, shifting their apparent hue in a consistent or locally bounded way.
concepts.name: color tinting

concepts.definition: Colors appear washed out, muted, gray, or reduced in chromatic intensity while visual brightness and clarity may remain separately intact.
concepts.name: color suppression

concepts.definition: Moving objects are seen as discrete jumps, freeze-frames, or missing intervals rather than as continuous motion.
concepts.name: visual motion discontinuity

concepts.definition: An inanimate visible object appears to move with self-directed or lifelike articulation, beyond simple drifting, breathing, or geometric deformation.
concepts.name: object animation

concepts.definition: Ordinary light is experienced as visually aversive, painful, or intolerably intense, rather than simply appearing brighter.
concepts.name: photophobia

concepts.definition: A misty, smoky, veiled, or fog-like layer appears across vision while object contours may remain more focused than in blurred vision.
concepts.name: visual haziness

concepts.definition: The visual field, an image, or a scene appears nested or repeated within itself, without requiring the scale-invariant geometry of fractal imagery.
concepts.name: visual recursion

concepts.definition: Letters, words, or lines appear to move, rearrange, detach, or lose stable visual organization despite still being experienced as text.
concepts.name: textual instability

concepts.definition: A broad fallback for a directly experienced change in hearing whose specific acoustic form cannot be determined; it does not mean merely liking or noticing sound.
concepts.name: auditory distortions

concepts.definition: Sound is experienced as globally richer, more vivid, detailed, or immersive, without enough evidence to isolate clarity, loudness, pitch, or another narrower dimension.
concepts.name: auditory enhancement

concepts.definition: Individual tones, voices, instruments, or acoustic details become unusually distinct and easy to resolve, independently of perceived loudness.
concepts.name: sound clarity enhancement

concepts.definition: External sounds are perceived as louder or more forceful than expected, without necessarily becoming clearer, richer, or more emotionally valued.
concepts.name: sound amplification

concepts.definition: External sounds seem quieter, muffled, distant, or reduced in impact despite no adequate change in the sound source.
concepts.name: sound dampening

concepts.definition: A sound is followed by one or more distinct perceived repetitions, separable from the continuous decaying resonance characteristic of reverberation.
concepts.name: echoing

concepts.definition: Sounds appear to persist and decay through an enlarged or unusually resonant acoustic space rather than returning as discrete repeats.
concepts.name: reverberation

concepts.definition: A sound's perceived frequency or melodic height shifts, bends, wobbles, or becomes unstable while the source remains otherwise identifiable.
concepts.name: pitch distortion

concepts.definition: Music, speech rhythm, or repeated sound appears faster, slower, or rhythmically displaced without a corresponding source change.
concepts.name: tempo distortion

concepts.definition: Individual sounds appear unnaturally stretched, shortened, arrested, or temporally smeared, distinct from a change in a sequence's overall tempo.
concepts.name: sound duration distortion

concepts.definition: The tonal color or texture of a sound changes, becoming metallic, phased, synthetic, hollow, or otherwise qualitatively unlike its familiar source.
concepts.name: timbre distortion

concepts.definition: Sound-like content is experienced internally and recognized as imagination or mental sound, rather than localized as an event in external auditory space.
concepts.name: auditory imagery

concepts.definition: A voice, tone, music, noise, or other sound is heard without an ordinary external source; the specific content belongs in detail.
concepts.name: auditory hallucination

concepts.definition: A real or perceived sound seems to originate from the wrong direction, distance, location, or spatial extent.
concepts.name: sound localization distortion

concepts.definition: A short sound, word, musical segment, or internally heard sequence repeats involuntarily with a recognizable cycle.
concepts.name: auditory looping

concepts.definition: Ambiguous real noise is heard as a voice, music, words, or another organized auditory object, rather than sound arising with no stimulus.
concepts.name: auditory pareidolia

concepts.definition: A broad fallback for a directly experienced alteration in smell whose specific direction or form cannot be established from the report.
concepts.name: olfactory change

concepts.definition: Existing odors seem unusually strong, vivid, differentiated, or easy to detect, without a new smell being perceived in their absence.
concepts.name: olfactory enhancement

concepts.definition: Existing odors become unusually faint, difficult to identify, or absent from awareness despite an expected source.
concepts.name: olfactory suppression

concepts.definition: A smell is perceived without an ordinary external odor source; its qualities, such as smoke or floral scent, belong in detail.
concepts.name: olfactory hallucination

concepts.definition: A present or familiar odor smells qualitatively altered, wrong, or unlike its usual character rather than merely stronger or weaker.
concepts.name: olfactory distortion

concepts.definition: A broad fallback for a directly experienced alteration in taste whose specific direction or form cannot be established from the report.
concepts.name: gustatory change

concepts.definition: Flavor or basic taste qualities seem unusually vivid, intense, differentiated, or easy to notice while an ordinary taste source is present.
concepts.name: taste enhancement

concepts.definition: Flavor or basic taste qualities seem unusually faint, muted, or absent despite food, drink, or another expected source.
concepts.name: taste suppression

concepts.definition: A taste is experienced without an ordinary source in the mouth; its metallic, bitter, chemical, or other content belongs in detail.
concepts.name: gustatory hallucination

concepts.definition: Food, drink, or another present source tastes qualitatively wrong or different from its familiar character, beyond a simple gain or loss of intensity.
concepts.name: taste distortion

concepts.definition: A broad fallback for an unusual coupling between sensory or conceptual categories when the report does not establish a specific synesthetic relation.
concepts.name: synesthetic change

concepts.definition: A stimulus or concept in one modality or category automatically evokes a concurrent experience in another; inducer and concurrent modalities belong in detail.
concepts.name: synesthesia

concepts.definition: A broad fallback for a directly experienced alteration in balance, gravity, acceleration, or bodily motion when no narrower vestibular effect is justified.
concepts.name: vestibular change

concepts.definition: The self or surroundings seem to rotate or spin despite no matching movement, distinct from non-rotational rocking, translation, or lightheadedness.
concepts.name: vertigo

concepts.definition: The body feels pushed, pulled, launched, or accelerated in a direction despite no matching change in physical velocity.
concepts.name: illusory acceleration

concepts.definition: The body feels lifted, suspended, or floating above its support despite remaining physically in place; this concerns vertical support rather than self-location.
concepts.name: illusory levitation

concepts.definition: A compelling bodily sensation of dropping or falling occurs without corresponding downward movement.
concepts.name: illusory falling

concepts.definition: The self feels translated, rocked, swayed, or moved despite physical stillness; rotational self or world motion is classified as vertigo.
concepts.name: illusory self-motion

concepts.definition: The direction or strength of gravity feels altered, tilted, reversed, absent, or multiplied, beyond a single sensation of falling or floating.
concepts.name: gravitational distortion

concepts.definition: A broad fallback for a directly experienced alteration in bodily position or internal-state awareness when its specific interoceptive or proprioceptive form is unclear.
concepts.name: body awareness change

concepts.definition: The felt position, shape, movement, or spatial arrangement of one's body or limbs differs from their actual configuration, independently of how they look.
concepts.name: proprioceptive distortion

concepts.definition: Ordinary signals from within the body, such as heartbeat, breathing, fullness, or visceral activity, enter awareness with unusually strong intensity or detail.
concepts.name: interoceptive amplification

concepts.definition: Ordinary signals from within the body become unusually faint, remote, or inaccessible to awareness without necessarily producing general numbness.
concepts.name: interoceptive attenuation

concepts.definition: Internal organs or bodily interiors feel displaced, reshaped, empty, enlarged, rearranged, or otherwise configured differently from their familiar felt organization.
concepts.name: visceral distortion

concepts.definition: Attention is unusually drawn to an otherwise ordinary-feeling heartbeat; forceful, racing, or irregular beats are instead palpitations.
concepts.name: cardiac awareness

concepts.definition: Breathing becomes unusually prominent in attention while remaining physically easy; air hunger or felt breathing difficulty is instead dyspnea.
concepts.name: respiratory awareness

concepts.definition: A broad fallback for a directly felt bodily burden or alteration that the report does not describe precisely enough for a narrower somatic effect.
concepts.name: body load

concepts.definition: The body or a body region feels unusually heavy, weighted, dense, or difficult to lift, whether or not actual strength is reduced.
concepts.name: somatic heaviness

concepts.definition: The body or a body region feels unusually light, buoyant, hollow, or nearly weightless, without necessarily creating an illusion of levitation.
concepts.name: somatic lightness

concepts.definition: The body feels physiologically activated, keyed up, or driven into heightened arousal; this is distinct from having comfortable strength or endurance.
concepts.name: stimulation

concepts.definition: The body and behavior feel pharmacologically slowed, subdued, or difficult to activate, beyond ordinary tiredness alone.
concepts.name: sedation

concepts.definition: A directly felt increase in bodily vigor, stamina, or capacity for exertion, without requiring tense arousal, restlessness, or compulsive activity.
concepts.name: physical energy

concepts.definition: Bodily or mental resources feel depleted, exhausted, or unable to sustain effort, distinct from calm sedation or simple sleepiness.
concepts.name: fatigue

concepts.definition: Remaining still feels difficult or uncomfortable and movement is desired, without the severe inner motor compulsion required for akathisia.
concepts.name: restlessness

concepts.definition: A distressing state of tense activation, irritability, or unsettled bodily arousal is felt, often but not necessarily accompanied by movement.
concepts.name: agitation

concepts.definition: A body part shakes with relatively rhythmic, repeated oscillation that is experienced or observed, rather than isolated twitches or larger sudden jerks.
concepts.name: tremor

concepts.definition: Skeletal muscles feel persistently contracted, rigid, clenched, or resistant to release, whether generalized or localized in detail.
concepts.name: muscle tension

concepts.definition: Skeletal muscles feel unusually loose, released, or free of habitual contraction without necessarily causing weakness or sedation.
concepts.name: muscle relaxation

concepts.definition: The jaw muscles feel clenched, tight, sore, or resistant to opening; actual repetitive tooth grinding or clenching is classified as bruxism.
concepts.name: jaw tension

concepts.definition: The teeth are involuntarily or compulsively ground or clenched, as an action rather than only a static sensation of jaw tightness.
concepts.name: bruxism

concepts.definition: A light prickling, sparkling, vibrating, or effervescent skin or bodily sensation is felt, without the sharper clustered quality of pins and needles.
concepts.name: tingling

concepts.definition: Numerous small, sharp prickling sensations resembling a limb waking from compression are felt in a localized or spreading region.
concepts.name: pins and needles

concepts.definition: Ordinary touch or bodily sensation is reduced or absent in a region, distinct from merely feeling emotionally detached from the body.
concepts.name: numbness

concepts.definition: The body or a region feels warmer than expected without necessarily showing skin redness, sweating, or a changing temperature.
concepts.name: warmth

concepts.definition: The body or a region feels colder than expected without necessarily involving shivering, goosebumps, or alternating temperature.
concepts.name: coldness

concepts.definition: Felt bodily temperature shifts back and forth, changes abruptly, or varies in waves rather than remaining consistently warm or cold.
concepts.name: temperature fluctuation

concepts.definition: A sudden spreading heat, redness, or hot rush is felt at the skin, commonly in the face or upper body, rather than diffuse steady warmth.
concepts.name: flushing

concepts.definition: Cold waves or shivering sensations pass through the body, whether or not ambient temperature is low or goosebumps are visible.
concepts.name: chills

concepts.definition: The skin's hairs seem to stand and small raised bumps are felt or observed, independently of whether fear, cold, music, or awe triggered them.
concepts.name: goosebumps

concepts.definition: A body area feels pushed upon, compressed, full, or under internal or external pressure without enough evidence for a narrower painful or visceral effect.
concepts.name: pressure sensation

concepts.definition: A body region feels constricted, bound, squeezed, or unable to expand normally, distinct from a clearly muscular contraction alone.
concepts.name: tightness

concepts.definition: The head feels faint, hollow, floating, or close to losing consciousness, without the false rotational motion that defines vertigo.
concepts.name: lightheadedness

concepts.definition: A nonspecific sense of unsteadiness, disorientation, or disequilibrium is felt when the report does not establish spinning vertigo or near-faint lightheadedness.
concepts.name: dizziness

concepts.definition: The body or a muscle group feels unable to produce normal force or support, whether or not objective power was tested.
concepts.name: weakness

concepts.definition: A sustained fine vibration or humming sensation seems to fill the body or a region, distinct from discrete shocks or surface-level prickling.
concepts.name: bodily buzzing

concepts.definition: Sudden shocks, currents, zaps, or electrically charged waves are felt moving through or across the body.
concepts.name: electric sensations

concepts.definition: The body feels unusually settled, easeful, well-positioned, or free of strain, distinct from an actively pleasurable bodily sensation.
concepts.name: physical comfort

concepts.definition: The body feels unpleasant, ill-at-ease, or physically wrong without a more specific localized symptom or clearly painful quality.
concepts.name: physical discomfort

concepts.definition: An unpleasant bodily sensation with aching, burning, stabbing, throbbing, or other painful quality is directly experienced; location and quality belong in detail.
concepts.name: pain

concepts.definition: Pre-existing or expected pain becomes noticeably reduced or absent, rather than attention simply moving away from an unchanged sensation.
concepts.name: pain relief

concepts.definition: Existing or provoked pain feels stronger, sharper, broader, or more intrusive than expected without a corresponding change in its source.
concepts.name: pain amplification

concepts.definition: A cutaneous irritation produces a direct urge or desire to scratch, whether localized, migrating, or generalized.
concepts.name: itching

concepts.definition: A directly felt pleasant bodily sensation or somatic euphoria occurs, distinct from positive mood, comfort alone, or appreciation of external touch.
concepts.name: bodily pleasure

concepts.definition: The heartbeat feels unusually forceful, fast, irregular, fluttering, skipping, or pounding, rather than merely receiving increased attention.
concepts.name: palpitations

concepts.definition: Breathing feels difficult, insufficient, effortful, tight, or air-hungry, distinct from simply becoming conscious of otherwise comfortable respiration.
concepts.name: dyspnea

concepts.definition: A diffuse bodily sense of sickness, unwellness, or physical debility is felt without a narrower symptom adequately accounting for it.
concepts.name: malaise

concepts.definition: A direct bodily desire or need to drink is unusually present, typically with felt dryness or a sense that fluid is needed.
concepts.name: thirst

concepts.definition: A sudden or unusually compelling need to urinate is felt, whether or not the bladder is full or urination follows.
concepts.name: urinary urgency

concepts.definition: Urination is difficult to initiate or complete despite a felt need or apparently full bladder, rather than the need itself being absent.
concepts.name: urinary retention

concepts.definition: Sweating becomes unusually increased, reduced, localized, or otherwise altered; its direction and body area belong in detail.
concepts.name: perspiration change

concepts.definition: A tactile sensation resembling insects crawling on or beneath the skin is felt without a matching external cause.
concepts.name: formication

concepts.definition: A broad fallback for a directly experienced alteration in voluntary movement, posture, or motor control when no narrower motor effect is established.
concepts.name: motor change

concepts.definition: Movements fail to combine smoothly or accurately, producing clumsy, poorly timed, or mismatched actions beyond a problem limited to balance or fine dexterity.
concepts.name: incoordination

concepts.definition: Maintaining upright posture or a stable stance becomes difficult, with swaying or instability that is not merely an illusory sensation of motion.
concepts.name: impaired balance

concepts.definition: Precise small movements, such as typing, writing, fastening, or manipulating objects, become unusually inaccurate or difficult.
concepts.name: impaired fine motor control

concepts.definition: A distressing inner motor restlessness creates a compelling need to move repeatedly and an inability to remain still, stronger than ordinary restlessness.
concepts.name: akathisia

concepts.definition: A specific movement or sequence is repeatedly performed with a felt drive or difficulty resisting it, rather than from generalized restlessness.
concepts.name: compulsive movement

concepts.definition: Voluntary movement markedly decreases because remaining motionless feels natural, absorbing, or preferred, while the capacity to move is retained.
concepts.name: stillness

concepts.definition: The person experiences being unable or nearly unable to initiate bodily movement despite wanting or attempting to move.
concepts.name: immobility

concepts.definition: Brief, localized, involuntary muscle contractions occur as small flicks or jumps, distinct from rhythmic tremor or larger whole-limb jerks.
concepts.name: muscle twitching

concepts.definition: Sudden, brief, involuntary movements displace a limb, body segment, or the whole body, rather than producing a regular oscillation.
concepts.name: jerking

concepts.definition: The eyes make involuntary repetitive oscillating or jerking movements, experienced directly or clearly reported as eye movement rather than visual-field vibration alone.
concepts.name: nystagmus

concepts.definition: Speech articulation becomes slurred, poorly coordinated, or mechanically difficult because the motor production of speech is impaired, not because words cannot be found.
concepts.name: dysarthria

concepts.definition: The body or limbs remain rigidly fixed in an imposed or adopted posture with markedly reduced spontaneous movement, beyond chosen stillness.
concepts.name: catalepsy

concepts.definition: A broad fallback for a directly experienced digestive, oral, or bowel change when the report does not justify a more specific gastrointestinal effect.
concepts.name: gastrointestinal effects

concepts.definition: A sick, queasy sensation with an urge or possibility of vomiting is felt, whether or not vomiting actually occurs.
concepts.name: nausea

concepts.definition: Stomach contents are forcefully expelled through the mouth or the report clearly describes throwing up, rather than nausea alone.
concepts.name: vomiting

concepts.definition: The stomach or upper abdomen feels unsettled, sore, heavy, or unpleasant without clear nausea, cramping, bloating, or reflux.
concepts.name: stomach discomfort

concepts.definition: Painful or uncomfortable involuntary contractions are felt in the abdomen or digestive tract, often arriving in waves rather than as diffuse discomfort.
concepts.name: cramping

concepts.definition: The abdomen feels swollen, distended, pressurized, or unusually full, whether or not visible enlargement or gas is present.
concepts.name: bloating

concepts.definition: Desire or willingness to eat is reduced or absent despite an ordinary opportunity or prior need for food.
concepts.name: loss of appetite

concepts.definition: Hunger, interest in food, or the desire to eat becomes stronger or more persistent than expected.
concepts.name: increased appetite

concepts.definition: The mouth feels unusually dry, sticky, or lacking saliva, independently of whether thirst is also present.
concepts.name: dry mouth

concepts.definition: Saliva production or the felt accumulation of saliva becomes unusually prominent or excessive, rather than ordinary mouth moisture.
concepts.name: salivation

concepts.definition: Initiating or completing a swallow feels unusually effortful, obstructed, uncoordinated, or unsafe, distinct from simple throat dryness.
concepts.name: difficulty swallowing

concepts.definition: Bowel movements become abnormally loose, watery, or frequent rather than merely urgent or accompanied by cramping.
concepts.name: diarrhea

concepts.definition: Passing stool becomes unusually infrequent, difficult, incomplete, or hard despite an apparent need or usual routine.
concepts.name: constipation

concepts.definition: A sudden, compelling need to defecate is felt and is difficult to defer, whether or not stool is loose or evacuation occurs.
concepts.name: bowel urgency

concepts.definition: Burning, acidic, or regurgitating stomach contents are felt rising into the chest, throat, or mouth, distinct from nonspecific stomach discomfort.
concepts.name: acid reflux

concepts.definition: Intestinal gas production, pressure, or passage becomes unusually prominent and is directly experienced or reported.
concepts.name: flatulence

concepts.definition: Repeated involuntary diaphragm contractions produce abrupt inspirations and characteristic hiccup sounds or sensations.
concepts.name: hiccups

concepts.definition: A broad fallback for a directly felt alteration in emotion or motivation when the report does not identify a more specific affective state.
concepts.name: emotional change

concepts.definition: A pronounced, often diffuse state of exceptional well-being, elation, or pleasure is felt, broader and more activated than simple contentment.
concepts.name: euphoria

concepts.definition: A distinct positive emotion of gladness or delight is felt in response to experience, without requiring the pervasive elevation of euphoria.
concepts.name: joy

concepts.definition: A quiet positive state of satisfaction and having enough is felt, with little pressure for circumstances to become different.
concepts.name: contentment

concepts.definition: A gentle affective glow of friendliness, care, or benevolence is felt, distinct from bodily heat and from attachment to one specific person.
concepts.name: emotional warmth

concepts.definition: Fondness, tenderness, or caring attachment is felt toward a particular person, being, or object, without necessarily reaching the intensity of love.
concepts.name: affection

concepts.definition: A strong affective experience of deep care, attachment, devotion, or valuing is felt toward another, oneself, or a clearly specified object.
concepts.name: love

concepts.definition: Another's suffering evokes caring concern and a wish for it to be relieved, distinct from merely understanding or sharing that person's state.
concepts.name: compassion

concepts.definition: Appreciative recognition is felt for a benefit, kindness, relationship, circumstance, or gift that is experienced as received rather than self-produced.
concepts.name: gratitude

concepts.definition: Tension or distress falls away because a feared, painful, or burdensome condition has ended, been avoided, or become less threatening.
concepts.name: relief

concepts.definition: Emotional and physiological agitation subsides into a low-arousal, steady state, without necessarily carrying the broader reconciliation implied by inner peace.
concepts.name: calmness

concepts.definition: A deep sense of internal harmony, reconciliation, and freedom from conflict is felt, extending beyond momentary relaxation or reduced arousal.
concepts.name: inner peace

concepts.definition: Uneasy anticipatory arousal, worry, tension, or threat sensitivity is felt even when the danger is uncertain, diffuse, or not immediately present.
concepts.name: anxiety

concepts.definition: Mild or focused unease is directed toward a possible upcoming event or outcome, distinct from diffuse anxiety and immediate fear.
concepts.name: apprehension

concepts.definition: An aversive emotion arises in response to a perceived immediate threat or danger, with an urge to escape, freeze, or protect oneself.
concepts.name: fear

concepts.definition: Fear or alarm escalates abruptly into an overwhelming acute state with felt loss of control or urgent need to escape.
concepts.name: panic

concepts.definition: A compelling feeling that catastrophe, death, or something terribly wrong is imminent occurs without the report necessarily identifying a concrete threat.
concepts.name: impending doom

concepts.definition: Other people or agents are believed or strongly suspected to intend harm, surveillance, deception, or conspiracy toward the self.
concepts.name: paranoia

concepts.definition: The threshold for annoyance is lowered so minor stimuli or frustrations provoke disproportionate impatience, tension, or readiness to become angry.
concepts.name: irritability

concepts.definition: A hostile, confrontational emotion is directed at a perceived wrong, obstruction, or offender, often with an urge to oppose or retaliate.
concepts.name: anger

concepts.definition: Aversion and tension arise because a goal, need, expectation, or action is blocked, without necessarily becoming anger toward an offender.
concepts.name: frustration

concepts.definition: A painful low-valence emotion of unhappiness, sorrow, or loss is felt, without requiring bereavement, hopelessness, or a prolonged mood.
concepts.name: sadness

concepts.definition: Sorrow is organized around a significant loss, separation, or death and may include yearning, pain, protest, or difficulty accepting that loss.
concepts.name: grief

concepts.definition: Emotions shift rapidly, repeatedly, or disproportionately over a short period, rather than one emotion merely being intense or easily evoked.
concepts.name: emotional lability

concepts.definition: The felt intensity, range, or responsiveness of emotion is broadly reduced, distinct from indifference toward one matter or loss of pleasure alone.
concepts.name: emotional blunting

concepts.definition: Emotions are triggered more readily or felt more strongly by ordinary events, without necessarily becoming unmanageable or rapidly changing.
concepts.name: emotional sensitivity

concepts.definition: Vastness, power, beauty, or significance evokes wonder together with a felt need to expand one's existing frame of understanding.
concepts.name: awe

concepts.definition: Open, absorbed amazement and curiosity are felt toward something striking or mysterious, without requiring the perceived vastness characteristic of awe.
concepts.name: wonder

concepts.definition: An event sharply violates expectation and produces a brief orienting emotional response, independently of whether the event is pleasant or unpleasant.
concepts.name: surprise

concepts.definition: Light, bubbly, excitable amusement or elation is felt with reduced seriousness or composure, rather than the broader well-being of euphoria.
concepts.name: giddiness

concepts.definition: Previously held or accumulated emotion is intensely expressed or released with a felt sense of discharge, completion, or subsequent relief.
concepts.name: emotional catharsis

concepts.definition: The person feels unable to influence, escape, or effectively respond to an important situation, even if possible actions objectively remain.
concepts.name: helplessness

concepts.definition: The motives, honesty, or safety of others are treated with increased doubt and guardedness, without a formed belief that they are persecuting the self.
concepts.name: suspiciousness

concepts.definition: Pre-existing anxiety, worry, or tense anticipation becomes noticeably reduced or absent, rather than calmness arising without a prior anxious state.
concepts.name: anxiety relief

concepts.definition: Fear tied to a particular threat or feared object becomes noticeably reduced or absent while that fear would otherwise be expected.
concepts.name: fear relief

concepts.definition: Emotionally colored longing or fond reflection is directed toward a personally meaningful past time, experience, culture, or earlier version of life.
concepts.name: nostalgia

concepts.definition: The whole self is felt to be bad, exposed, defective, or unworthy in the eyes of self or others, rather than one action alone being judged wrong.
concepts.name: shame

concepts.definition: Distress and self-reproach are directed toward a specific action, omission, or responsibility experienced as morally or personally wrong.
concepts.name: guilt

concepts.definition: Acute self-conscious discomfort follows an awkward mistake, exposure, or social norm breach, usually without the global self-condemnation of shame.
concepts.name: embarrassment

concepts.definition: A strong aversive reaction of revulsion and rejection occurs toward something experienced as contaminating, offensive, bodily repellent, or morally foul.
concepts.name: disgust

concepts.definition: Another person or group is regarded with scornful devaluation, inferiority, or unworthiness, distinct from anger at a specific harmful act.
concepts.name: contempt

concepts.definition: A diffuse, unpleasant affective state of unease, dissatisfaction, or feeling emotionally bad is present without resolving into one narrower negative emotion.
concepts.name: dysphoria

concepts.definition: Activities or experiences that are normally rewarding fail to produce anticipated or consummatory pleasure, distinct from lacking motivation to begin them.
concepts.name: anhedonia

concepts.definition: Interest, concern, and emotional or motivational engagement are broadly diminished, even where pleasure may still be possible if activity occurs.
concepts.name: apathy

concepts.definition: Positive change or a tolerable future feels unavailable or impossible, distinct from sadness about present circumstances alone.
concepts.name: hopelessness

concepts.definition: The intensity or quantity of emotion exceeds the person's felt capacity to process, regulate, or contain it, regardless of which emotion is present.
concepts.name: emotional overwhelm

concepts.definition: Positive or mixed anticipatory arousal builds around an upcoming or unfolding event, carrying energy and eagerness rather than diffuse euphoria.
concepts.name: excitement

concepts.definition: Confidence in one's ability to act, decide, perform, or cope becomes stronger, distinct from a global increase in personal worth.
concepts.name: self-confidence elevation

concepts.definition: The person's overall evaluation of their own worth, value, or adequacy becomes more positive, independently of confidence in one task.
concepts.name: self-esteem elevation

concepts.definition: The willingness and drive to initiate or sustain goal-directed action increase, without requiring elevated mood or physical energy.
concepts.name: motivation enhancement

concepts.definition: The willingness or drive to initiate and sustain goal-directed action decreases, even if the goal remains valued and physical capacity is present.
concepts.name: motivation suppression

concepts.definition: The current situation feels under-stimulating, unengaging, and difficult to remain interested in, often with a desire for different activity.
concepts.name: boredom

concepts.definition: The desire to explore, ask questions, seek information, or understand unfamiliar material becomes unusually strong or broadly available.
concepts.name: curiosity enhancement

concepts.definition: The person's overall evaluation of their own worth, value, or adequacy becomes more negative, beyond uncertainty about one ability or action.
concepts.name: self-esteem suppression

concepts.definition: Waiting, repetition, delay, or slow progress becomes easier to tolerate without frustration or pressure to accelerate the process.
concepts.name: patience enhancement

concepts.definition: Waiting, repetition, delay, or slow progress becomes unusually difficult to tolerate and provokes impatience or pressure for immediate change.
concepts.name: patience suppression

concepts.definition: A focused, compelling desire for a substance, reward, activity, or experience is felt with motivational pull beyond ordinary preference.
concepts.name: craving

concepts.definition: A painful discrepancy is felt between desired and actual social connection, even when other people are physically present.
concepts.name: loneliness

concepts.definition: Heavy, sustained aversion and fear are directed toward an anticipated event or future, distinct from the abrupt certainty that catastrophe is imminent.
concepts.name: dread

concepts.definition: A difficult fact, feeling, limitation, or circumstance is allowed to be present without continued internal resistance, denial, or demand that it differ.
concepts.name: acceptance

concepts.definition: The self feels emotionally exposed, undefended, or open to being affected or hurt, whether experienced as welcome, frightening, or both.
concepts.name: vulnerability

concepts.definition: Something is experienced as funny, playful, or entertaining and evokes enjoyment or laughter, without requiring generalized happiness.
concepts.name: amusement

concepts.definition: Another's possession, quality, status, or advantage evokes painful wanting for the same thing, distinct from fear of losing an existing bond.
concepts.name: envy

concepts.definition: A valued relationship or position feels threatened by a rival, producing fear, insecurity, anger, or possessiveness.
concepts.name: jealousy

concepts.definition: Persistent anger or bitterness is held over perceived unfair treatment, insult, or unmet obligation and remains directed toward its source.
concepts.name: resentment

concepts.definition: A past choice, action, or missed possibility is wished different, with painful counterfactual awareness of what might have occurred instead.
concepts.name: regret

concepts.definition: Hostility, resentment, or demand for repayment toward an offender is voluntarily or emotionally released without requiring approval of the offense.
concepts.name: forgiveness

concepts.definition: One's importance, certainty, or abilities are held in balanced perspective without self-aggrandizement, while personal worth need not be diminished.
concepts.name: humility

concepts.definition: Personal pain, failure, or limitation is met with increased kindness, understanding, and common-humanity perspective rather than harsh self-judgment.
concepts.name: self-compassion enhancement

concepts.definition: Beauty, form, harmony, artistry, or sensory composition is valued and emotionally appreciated more strongly, regardless of whether the object is music, nature, or art.
concepts.name: aesthetic appreciation

concepts.definition: Favorable outcomes and positive future possibilities feel more plausible or expected than usual, without requiring certainty or elevated self-confidence.
concepts.name: optimism enhancement

concepts.definition: Unfavorable outcomes and negative future possibilities feel especially plausible or expected, without necessarily reaching the impossibility implied by hopelessness.
concepts.name: pessimism

concepts.definition: A light, exploratory willingness to joke, improvise, experiment, or engage without rigid instrumental purpose becomes prominent.
concepts.name: playfulness

concepts.definition: People, memories, symbols, or objects evoke unusually tender and emotionally idealized feeling, often because of their personal associations.
concepts.name: sentimentality

concepts.definition: A soft, gentle, protective affection is felt toward someone or something perceived as precious or vulnerable.
concepts.name: tenderness

concepts.definition: The person directly feels protected, secure, and free from immediate threat, beyond merely thinking that the environment is objectively safe.
concepts.name: sense of safety

concepts.definition: The person more readily identifies and condemns their own perceived faults, errors, or inadequacies, with an unusually harsh evaluative stance.
concepts.name: self-criticism enhancement

concepts.definition: An unresolved event, relationship, question, or emotional process feels complete enough to release continued searching, protest, or unfinished tension.
concepts.name: closure

concepts.definition: Perceived criticism or threat to self-image evokes increased denial, justification, counterattack, or resistance to considering the information.
concepts.name: defensiveness

concepts.definition: The self, including flaws, history, body, or current condition, is regarded with less rejection and less demand to become someone else.
concepts.name: self-acceptance

concepts.definition: A particular outcome, issue, person, or choice carries little preference or emotional concern, without implying globally reduced motivation or feeling.
concepts.name: indifference

concepts.definition: A reflective, subdued, often bittersweet sadness colors experience without requiring a specific recent loss or the acute pain of grief.
concepts.name: melancholy

concepts.definition: Distress and longing are directed toward home, familiar surroundings, or the people associated with them while one feels separated from that home.
concepts.name: homesickness

concepts.definition: A specific desire for closeness, reunion, intimacy, or connection with another person is felt, distinct from diffuse loneliness.
concepts.name: relational longing

concepts.definition: Pleasure is felt while imagining or expecting a future rewarding experience, before the reward itself is occurring.
concepts.name: anticipatory pleasure

concepts.definition: Attention deliberately or spontaneously dwells on a present or remembered positive experience in a way that prolongs and deepens its enjoyment.
concepts.name: savoring

concepts.definition: The capacity to engage, empathize, or regulate feeling seems depleted after sustained emotional demand, distinct from general physical fatigue.
concepts.name: emotional exhaustion

concepts.definition: Thinking about or performing a particular task evokes disproportionate resistance, unpleasantness, or urge to avoid it, beyond low motivation in general.
concepts.name: task aversion

concepts.definition: Witnessing or contemplating exemplary goodness evokes uplift, warmth, admiration, and motivation to act more prosocially oneself.
concepts.name: moral elevation

concepts.definition: Satisfaction and positive self-evaluation arise from one's achievement, identity, relationship, or valued contribution, without necessarily implying superiority.
concepts.name: pride

concepts.definition: Sadness or dissatisfaction follows when an expected or hoped-for outcome fails to occur or falls short of its anticipated value.
concepts.name: disappointment

concepts.definition: A desire to punish, retaliate against, or make an offender suffer is felt in response to a perceived injury or humiliation.
concepts.name: vindictiveness

concepts.definition: A pervasive, enduring sense of injustice hardens into bitterness and grievance that colors broader life experience beyond one episode of resentment.
concepts.name: embitterment

concepts.definition: Another person, ability, action, or object is regarded with warm approval and esteem for an excellence or value it is perceived to possess.
concepts.name: admiration

concepts.definition: Positive feeling arises from another person's pleasure, happiness, or valued connection, especially where jealousy might otherwise be expected.
concepts.name: compersion

concepts.definition: Pleasure or satisfaction is felt in response to another person's misfortune, failure, or loss, whether or not harm was desired beforehand.
concepts.name: schadenfreude

concepts.definition: Opposing positive and negative evaluations or desires toward the same object coexist, making the person's stance genuinely mixed rather than merely uncertain.
concepts.name: ambivalence

concepts.definition: A felt emotion conflicts with its expression, the situation, or another simultaneously experienced affect; this is not rapid mood change.
concepts.name: emotional incongruence

concepts.definition: A firm emotional commitment to persist toward a chosen goal is felt despite difficulty, delay, or competing impulses.
concepts.name: determination

concepts.definition: The person feels able and willing to act in line with values or goals despite recognized fear, danger, or vulnerability.
concepts.name: courage

concepts.definition: A broad fallback for a directly experienced alteration in thinking, attention, memory, language, or executive function when no narrower cognitive effect is established.
concepts.name: cognitive change

concepts.definition: Information, events, or the current situation cannot be organized or understood coherently, producing uncertainty about what is happening or how elements relate.
concepts.name: confusion

concepts.definition: Thinking feels unusually lucid, coherent, precise, and easy to follow, without necessarily becoming faster, more analytical, or more focused.
concepts.name: mental clarity

concepts.definition: Thinking feels clouded, indistinct, slowed in access, or difficult to bring into clear focus, even when basic orientation and understanding remain.
concepts.name: foggy thinking

concepts.definition: Thoughts move through awareness at an unusually rapid pace, distinct from having many crowded thoughts at once or rapidly shifting topics.
concepts.name: racing thoughts

concepts.definition: Thoughts feel crowded, excessive, forcefully numerous, or difficult to contain; unlike racing thoughts, the defining feature is density and pressure rather than speed.
concepts.name: thought pressure

concepts.definition: The progression, formation, or retrieval of thoughts feels unusually slow, with extended gaps or effort between mental steps.
concepts.name: thought slowing

concepts.definition: The same thought, phrase, question, or short sequence repeats in a recognizable cycle, rather than sustained analysis of a broader concern.
concepts.name: thought looping

concepts.definition: Irrelevant thoughts intrude into and disrupt the current line of thinking without necessarily being unwanted, emotionally charged, or repetitive.
concepts.name: thought interference

concepts.definition: Attention is readily captured and diverted by competing internal or external stimuli, making the current task or thought difficult to sustain.
concepts.name: distractibility

concepts.definition: Attention repeatedly returns to and elaborates a distressing topic, problem, feeling, or past event without reaching resolution.
concepts.name: rumination

concepts.definition: A thought, doubt, image, or concern becomes persistent, intrusive, and difficult to disengage from, often with felt compulsion or disproportionate importance.
concepts.name: obsessive thinking

concepts.definition: Encoding, retaining, or retrieving information becomes broadly less reliable, when the report does not isolate working, prospective, autobiographical, or complete memory loss.
concepts.name: memory impairment

concepts.definition: Information or past experiences can be encoded, retained, or retrieved with unusual ease, detail, speed, or breadth.
concepts.name: memory enhancement

concepts.definition: Understanding, selecting, arranging, or producing words becomes unusually difficult, beyond a purely motor problem with articulating speech.
concepts.name: language impairment

concepts.definition: Spoken language is produced with unusually easy word access, continuity, articulation, or expressive flow, without merely increasing how much is said.
concepts.name: speech fluency enhancement

concepts.definition: Breaking information into parts, comparing alternatives, tracing causes, or following logical relations feels unusually effective or detailed.
concepts.name: analysis enhancement

concepts.definition: Access to and examination of one's own thoughts, motives, emotions, or patterns becomes unusually detailed, sustained, or revealing.
concepts.name: introspection enhancement

concepts.definition: Ideas, memories, words, or perceptions connect in new and unexpected ways that remain experienced as associations rather than literal external relations.
concepts.name: novel associations

concepts.definition: Experience is organized primarily through abstract concepts, categories, and relations rather than concrete sensory particulars or practical steps.
concepts.name: conceptual thinking

concepts.definition: Ideas, expectations, instructions, or cues from others more readily shape perception, belief, memory, or action than they ordinarily would.
concepts.name: suggestibility

concepts.definition: Usual restraints on speech, emotion, impulse, or behavior weaken, making actions or disclosures easier to express without adequate filtering.
concepts.name: reduced inhibition

concepts.definition: Attention can be deliberately sustained on a chosen object or task with reduced interference, without peripheral awareness necessarily disappearing.
concepts.name: increased focus

concepts.definition: Deliberate attention is difficult to maintain on a chosen object or task, even when no specific distractor repeatedly captures it.
concepts.name: decreased focus

concepts.definition: Attention becomes fully engrossed in an object or activity while peripheral, self, or time awareness recedes; ordinary concentration alone is increased focus.
concepts.name: attentional absorption

concepts.definition: The sequence and connections among thoughts lose coherent structure, becoming fragmented, tangential, loosely connected, or difficult for the thinker to follow.
concepts.name: thought disorganization

concepts.definition: Awareness temporarily contains no accessible thought or mental content despite an attempt or expectation to think, rather than one thought abruptly stopping.
concepts.name: mind blanking

concepts.definition: A false or implausible proposition is held with strong conviction despite inadequate evidence or clear contradiction, rather than entertained symbolically or hypothetically.
concepts.name: delusional thinking

concepts.definition: Neutral events, media, gestures, or coincidences seem specifically directed at or about the self, beyond ordinary personal relevance.
concepts.name: ideas of reference

concepts.definition: Beliefs about exceptional power, ability, knowledge, status, or destiny become markedly inflated, distinct from the experiential expansion of ego inflation.
concepts.name: grandiosity

concepts.definition: Attention persistently scans for danger or important change with heightened alertness and difficulty relaxing, often amplifying ambiguous threat cues.
concepts.name: hypervigilance

concepts.definition: The mind feels driven to assign significance, explanation, or hidden connection to experiences even when evidence is sparse and disengagement is difficult.
concepts.name: compulsive meaning-making

concepts.definition: Choosing among available options feels impossible or repeatedly stalls because evaluation cannot be concluded, despite retaining the physical ability to act.
concepts.name: decision paralysis

concepts.definition: The mind is experienced as divided into simultaneously active, conflicting streams, positions, or agents rather than merely feeling indecisive.
concepts.name: internal cognitive split

concepts.definition: A thought or belief continues to feel compelling while another level of awareness recognizes that it is illogical, implausible, or unsupported.
concepts.name: meta-awareness of irrationality

concepts.definition: An anomalous or delusion-like framework and ordinary practical reality are maintained in parallel without being fully reconciled or one simply displacing the other.
concepts.name: double bookkeeping

concepts.definition: A present situation feels as though it has already been experienced despite recognition that the familiarity is unwarranted or cannot be sourced.
concepts.name: déjà vu

concepts.definition: A familiar person, place, word, or situation temporarily feels novel or unrecognized despite factual knowledge that it is familiar.
concepts.name: jamais vu

concepts.definition: Generating original, useful, expressive, or imaginatively varied ideas feels easier or more productive than usual, beyond making novel associations alone.
concepts.name: creativity enhancement

concepts.definition: A previously inaccessible, neglected, or long-unrecalled memory returns spontaneously with recognizable autobiographical content; vividness belongs in detail.
concepts.name: memory resurfacing

concepts.definition: A bounded period, event, or body of information cannot be recalled at all or is experienced as missing, beyond ordinary forgetfulness.
concepts.name: amnesia

concepts.definition: Thinking, understanding, or the occurrence of ideas is itself directly pleasurable, independently of whether the ideas concern pleasant content.
concepts.name: ideational pleasure

concepts.definition: The usual stream of verbal self-talk becomes markedly quiet or absent while awareness and nonverbal experience continue.
concepts.name: internal monologue suppression

concepts.definition: Unwanted thoughts, images, or impulses enter awareness involuntarily and disrupt it, without requiring the repetition or fixed concern of obsessive thinking.
concepts.name: intrusive thoughts

concepts.definition: Ambiguous or manageable circumstances are rapidly interpreted through severe worst-case outcomes, with escalating predictions of disaster.
concepts.name: catastrophic thinking

concepts.definition: A memory gap is unknowingly filled with invented or distorted content that is experienced as genuine recollection rather than deliberate fabrication.
concepts.name: confabulation

concepts.definition: Thoughts occurring in one's own stream lack the ordinary felt quality of being mine, without necessarily being attributed to an outside inserter.
concepts.name: thought ownership loss

concepts.definition: A thought is experienced as placed into the mind by an external agent or source rather than generated by oneself.
concepts.name: thought insertion

concepts.definition: One's thoughts seem directly accessible, transmitted, or audible to other people without ordinary speech or communication.
concepts.name: thought broadcasting

concepts.definition: A thought is experienced as repeated, duplicated, or echoed shortly after it occurs, within the mind or as a percept-like recurrence.
concepts.name: thought echo

concepts.definition: Inner speech acquires perceptual or voice-like qualities and seems spatially external or heard, while remaining recognizable as related to one's own thinking.
concepts.name: inner speech externalization

concepts.definition: Actions or choices are initiated rapidly in response to immediate urges with reduced pause, deliberation, or consideration of consequences.
concepts.name: impulsivity

concepts.definition: Potential danger or negative consequences feel less probable, severe, or personally relevant than the situation warrants, independently of willingness to face known risk.
concepts.name: risk perception suppression

concepts.definition: Voluntarily or spontaneously imagined sights and scenes become unusually vivid, detailed, stable, or easy to manipulate while remaining recognized as mental imagery.
concepts.name: mental imagery enhancement

concepts.definition: An active train of thought stops abruptly and involuntarily before completion, leaving a discrete gap rather than gradually becoming faint.
concepts.name: thought blocking

concepts.definition: A thought progressively loses clarity, force, or accessibility before it can be completed, unlike the sudden cutoff of thought blocking.
concepts.name: thought fading

concepts.definition: The origin of a thought, memory, perception, or statement becomes difficult to identify, such as confusing imagined, heard, remembered, and self-generated material.
concepts.name: source monitoring impairment

concepts.definition: Thoughts, symbols, rituals, or unrelated events are treated as capable of causing or controlling outcomes through nonordinary connections.
concepts.name: magical thinking

concepts.definition: A response, word, action, topic, or cognitive operation continues or recurs after the context requires shifting away from it.
concepts.name: perseveration

concepts.definition: Strategies, interpretations, rules, or viewpoints are difficult to revise despite changed evidence or demands, beyond one repeated response.
concepts.name: cognitive rigidity

concepts.definition: The ability to monitor, evaluate, or recognize the reliability and process of one's own thinking becomes reduced.
concepts.name: metacognitive impairment

concepts.definition: Thoughts and feelings are observed as temporary mental events rather than automatically treated as facts, commands, or the whole self.
concepts.name: cognitive decentering

concepts.definition: Normally tacit aspects of thinking, perceiving, acting, or selfhood become objects of involuntary explicit attention, disrupting their transparent immediacy.
concepts.name: hyperreflexivity

concepts.definition: A repeatedly attended or repeated word temporarily loses its felt meaning and becomes an unfamiliar sound or visual form despite intact factual knowledge.
concepts.name: semantic satiation

concepts.definition: A stimulus, idea, or topic stands out as unusually important, attention-worthy, or significant; its particular content belongs in detail.
concepts.name: salience enhancement

concepts.definition: Awareness contracts around a limited object, cue, or concern while other available information is excluded, whether or not focus on the target improves.
concepts.name: attentional narrowing

concepts.definition: Forming, sequencing, and updating the steps needed to reach a goal becomes unusually difficult, even when the goal and individual actions are understood.
concepts.name: planning impairment

concepts.definition: The ability to voluntarily form or sustain internal visual or multisensory images becomes weaker or temporarily unavailable.
concepts.name: mental imagery suppression

concepts.definition: The ability to evaluate whether a perception, belief, or interpretation corresponds to shared external reality becomes reduced.
concepts.name: reality testing impairment

concepts.definition: Knowledge of current time, place, situation, or personal context becomes uncertain or incorrect, beyond a changed subjective sense of time.
concepts.name: orientation impairment

concepts.definition: The world or situation feels fundamentally puzzling and difficult to make sense of despite continued alert attention, rather than mere lack of information.
concepts.name: perplexity

concepts.definition: A personally meaningful pattern in one's emotions, motives, relationships, or behavior is newly recognized with a felt increase in self-understanding.
concepts.name: psychological insight

concepts.definition: The ability to translate an intention into chosen mental or bodily action feels reduced, even though the desired action and its goal remain known.
concepts.name: volitional control impairment

concepts.definition: The person knows that an affective change is present but has unusual difficulty distinguishing, naming, or understanding which emotion it is.
concepts.name: emotion identification difficulty

concepts.definition: Thinking follows loose, image-driven, discontinuous, or narratively improbable relations resembling dream mentation while the person is awake.
concepts.name: dreamlike cognition

concepts.definition: The mind repeatedly or vividly simulates how past or present events could have unfolded differently, without requiring regret about those alternatives.
concepts.name: counterfactual thinking

concepts.definition: A broad sequence of autobiographical memories or life periods is rapidly or panoramically revisited as an organized survey of one's life.
concepts.name: life review

concepts.definition: Thought rapidly shifts between topics through understandable but accelerating associations, distinct from simple speed within one line of thought.
concepts.name: flight of ideas

concepts.definition: A markedly increased and difficult-to-resist drive to write or produce extended written material is experienced, beyond ordinary creative productivity.
concepts.name: hypergraphia

concepts.definition: Existing assumptions and convictions become easier to reconsider, revise, or hold provisionally in light of alternatives or new evidence.
concepts.name: belief flexibility enhancement

concepts.definition: Information cannot be reliably held and manipulated over the few moments needed for ongoing thought or action, even if long-term memory remains intact.
concepts.name: working memory impairment

concepts.definition: An intention to perform a future action is forgotten at the relevant moment, such as losing why one entered a room or what one meant to do.
concepts.name: prospective memory impairment

concepts.definition: Disengaging from one task or mental set and reconfiguring attention for another becomes unusually slow, difficult, or unsuccessful.
concepts.name: task switching impairment

concepts.definition: Written words may remain visually legible yet their sentences, implications, or connected meaning become unusually difficult to understand.
concepts.name: reading comprehension impairment

concepts.definition: Recognizing, comparing, calculating, or reasoning with numbers becomes unusually difficult despite ordinary familiarity with the required operation.
concepts.name: numeracy impairment

concepts.definition: Ideas and perceptions are more readily organized through analogy, symbol, or figurative correspondence while those relations remain understood as metaphorical.
concepts.name: metaphorical thinking enhancement

concepts.definition: Situations, conventions, existence, or one's own actions appear strikingly incongruous, nonsensical, or absurd, often without a discrete factual contradiction.
concepts.name: absurdity perception

concepts.definition: Claims, assumptions, and apparent evidence are questioned more readily and held to a higher threshold before being accepted as true.
concepts.name: skepticism enhancement

concepts.definition: Ambiguity becomes difficult to tolerate and the mind repeatedly seeks definitive answers, reassurance, or closure before it can disengage.
concepts.name: certainty seeking

concepts.definition: The mind more actively and vividly simulates likely future states, consequences, or branching scenarios in order to anticipate what comes next.
concepts.name: predictive thinking enhancement

concepts.definition: Ordinary thinking, comprehension, or mental calculation feels unusually laborious and resource-demanding, even when accuracy is preserved.
concepts.name: cognitive effort amplification

concepts.definition: Thinking, comprehension, or mental calculation feels unusually effortless and fluent, without necessarily becoming more accurate or profound.
concepts.name: cognitive effort reduction

concepts.definition: Words, statements, or situations are interpreted more directly and concretely, with reduced spontaneous use of implication, irony, or figurative meaning.
concepts.name: literal thinking enhancement

concepts.definition: General principles, categories, hypothetical relations, or ideas removed from concrete examples become unusually difficult to form or understand.
concepts.name: abstraction difficulty

concepts.definition: A broad fallback for a directly experienced alteration in the pace, continuity, direction, or organization of time when no narrower temporal structure is established.
concepts.name: time distortion

concepts.definition: Time seems to pass more slowly than external events or clocks indicate, so moments or intervals feel unusually prolonged.
concepts.name: time dilation

concepts.definition: Time seems to pass more quickly than external events or clocks indicate, so substantial intervals feel unusually brief or compressed.
concepts.name: time contraction

concepts.definition: The ordinary sense of temporal passage or location disappears, leaving experience outside or independent of past, present, and future.
concepts.name: timelessness

concepts.definition: The continuity of lived time breaks into disconnected moments, segments, gaps, or jumps rather than one smoothly unfolding stream.
concepts.name: time fragmentation

concepts.definition: A span of events or the present moment feels as though it repeats cyclically, even when the person may know that external events are progressing.
concepts.name: looping sense of time

concepts.definition: The direction of temporal flow seems reversed, with events or lived succession appearing to move backward rather than merely being remembered in reverse order.
concepts.name: time reversal

concepts.definition: Temporal flow seems completely arrested at a single enduring moment, distinct from timelessness in which temporal structure is absent altogether.
concepts.name: time stoppage

concepts.definition: Events or periods ordinarily separated as past, present, or future are experienced as occurring together within one present field.
concepts.name: temporal simultaneity

concepts.definition: The before-and-after sequence of experiences becomes unclear, rearranged, or impossible to establish, without necessarily changing their perceived speed or direction.
concepts.name: temporal ordering disruption

concepts.definition: A broad fallback for an alteration in the experienced organization or extent of space when no more specific spatial structure is supported.
concepts.name: spatial change

concepts.definition: Experienced space itself feels globally enlarged, compressed, miniature, or vast, rather than one visible object's size or distance changing.
concepts.name: spatial scale distortion

concepts.definition: Space is experienced as limitless or extending without edges, enclosure, or reachable boundary while spatial extension still remains present.
concepts.name: spatial boundlessness

concepts.definition: Spatial extension or dimensionality seems absent altogether, distinct from very large, boundaryless, flattened, or visually empty space.
concepts.name: spacelessness

concepts.definition: Experienced perspective loses a single determinate spatial viewpoint, seeming nowhere, everywhere, or multiply located while the self remains embodied; bodily separation is disembodiment.
concepts.name: perspectival dislocation

concepts.definition: A broad fallback for a directly felt change in how the surrounding world presents as a whole, when no narrower world-experience structure is established.
concepts.name: world-experience change

concepts.definition: Familiar surroundings or situations feel subtly strange, eerie, or not-quite-right without a specific threat message, recognition failure, or sensory distortion.
concepts.name: uncanniness

concepts.definition: The entire situation carries an impending, charged sense that something momentous is about to happen, without a definite event or belief supplying that meaning.
concepts.name: atmospheric portent

concepts.definition: The surrounding world appears experientially drained of life, animation, warmth, or expressive presence, rather than simply visually dim or emotionally disliked.
concepts.name: environmental vitality loss

concepts.definition: Objects remain perceptually recognizable yet seem stripped of ordinary significance, function, or implicit meaning, distinct from language or memory impairment.
concepts.name: perceptual meaning loss

concepts.definition: Ordinary objects or surroundings present with a striking first-time freshness or novelty despite still being correctly recognized as familiar.
concepts.name: perceptual freshness

concepts.definition: A person, place, object, or situation feels far more familiar than recognition evidence warrants, distinct from merely remembering it clearly.
concepts.name: hyperfamiliarity

concepts.definition: A broad fallback for a directly experienced alteration in self, identity, embodiment, ownership, or agency when no narrower selfhood structure is established.
concepts.name: selfhood change

concepts.definition: A nonspecific detachment or disconnection occurs among awareness, emotion, memory, body, self, or surroundings when the report does not justify a narrower dissociative phenomenon.
concepts.name: dissociation

concepts.definition: The self, thoughts, emotions, or actions feel unreal, remote, mechanical, or observed from a distance while reality testing may remain intact.
concepts.name: depersonalization

concepts.definition: The surrounding world feels unreal, dreamlike, distant, artificial, or lacking ordinary immediacy despite continued recognition of the environment.
concepts.name: derealization

concepts.definition: The ordinary sense of a bounded, central, stable self becomes more permeable or less rigid while a recognizable self still remains.
concepts.name: ego softening

concepts.definition: The ordinary sense of being a distinct, bounded self substantially or completely disappears, rather than merely becoming flexible, small, or less important.
concepts.name: ego dissolution

concepts.definition: The experienced self feels expanded, enlarged, powerful, or all-encompassing, distinct from a propositional belief in exceptional status or ability.
concepts.name: ego inflation

concepts.definition: The experiential boundary separating self from another person, being, or environment becomes indistinct or absent while the relata may still be discernible.
concepts.name: loss of self-other boundary

concepts.definition: Uncertainty or incoherence arises about who one presently is, which identity is one's own, or how current self-aspects fit together.
concepts.name: identity confusion

concepts.definition: The self is experienced from a detached third-person or witness-like viewpoint, as though watching oneself rather than simply acting from the usual first person.
concepts.name: observer perspective

concepts.definition: The center of self or awareness feels located outside, above, or apart from the physical body, without requiring a visible bodily double.
concepts.name: disembodiment

concepts.definition: Self, others, nature, or reality are experienced as one undivided whole through loss or softening of ordinary separation, beyond interpersonal closeness alone.
concepts.name: unity experience

concepts.definition: The self or body is directly experienced as transforming into, becoming, or possessing the form of an animal; symbolic identification alone is insufficient.
concepts.name: theriomorphosis

concepts.definition: The ordinary felt authorship or control of one's actions, choices, or mental activity diminishes without an external controller necessarily being inferred.
concepts.name: agency loss

concepts.definition: One's body performs an action without a preceding felt decision or conscious initiation, as though the movement executes by itself.
concepts.name: action automaticity

concepts.definition: An outside person, force, entity, or mechanism seems to control one's actions, impulses, or experience, adding an attributed controller beyond agency loss.
concepts.name: external control experience

concepts.definition: An emotion occurring within experience lacks the ordinary felt quality of being one's own, without necessarily being attributed to an outside source.
concepts.name: affect ownership loss

concepts.definition: The felt identity shifts among different self-states, roles, traits, or modes with unusual ease, rather than merely becoming uncertain or less bounded.
concepts.name: identity fluidity

concepts.definition: More than one simultaneous self, center of subjectivity, or version of oneself is directly experienced, distinct from conflicting thoughts within one self.
concepts.name: self-multiplication

concepts.definition: The self or body is directly experienced as becoming an inanimate object, substance, process, or nonliving form rather than merely resembling it metaphorically.
concepts.name: inanimate self-transformation

concepts.definition: A visual double or image of one's own body is seen in external space while self-location remains anchored in the physical body.
concepts.name: autoscopy

concepts.definition: A bodily double is perceived while self-location, perspective, or identity alternates or becomes ambiguous between the physical body and the double.
concepts.name: heautoscopy

concepts.definition: The person directly experiences having died, undergoing death, or crossing a death transition, rather than merely fearing, imagining, or thinking about death.
concepts.name: felt death

concepts.definition: The body or a body part feels alien, not mine, borrowed, or owned by someone else despite remaining perceptually and anatomically present.
concepts.name: body ownership distortion

concepts.definition: One's mirror reflection is seen but feels unfamiliar, other, or not oneself, distinct from seeing a bodily double elsewhere in space.
concepts.name: mirror self-recognition disturbance

concepts.definition: The current self feels subjectively younger or childlike, with a younger mode of being rather than only recalling childhood events.
concepts.name: age regression

concepts.definition: The felt connection linking present self, past self, and personal life story becomes broken or unreal despite access to autobiographical facts.
concepts.name: personal continuity disruption
