concepts.definition: The internal appraisal or mental representation of one's bodily appearance becomes altered, distinct from visual size distortion or loss of bodily ownership.
concepts.name: body image distortion

concepts.definition: The directly felt gendered character of the self changes, broadens, or moves relative to its usual state; direction and context belong in detail.
concepts.name: gender identity shift

concepts.definition: One's own name feels strange, arbitrary, detached, or no longer expressive of oneself despite recognizing that it is factually one's name.
concepts.name: name alienation

concepts.definition: The experienced self feels extremely small, reduced, or insignificant in relation to something vast, distinct from low self-worth or balanced humility.
concepts.name: self-diminishment

concepts.definition: The basic felt immediacy of existing as the subject of experience becomes faint, distant, or barely there without disappearing entirely.
concepts.name: diminished self-presence

concepts.definition: The person feels more genuine, real, congruent, or true to their own values and identity, distinct from simply approving of themselves.
concepts.name: authenticity enhancement

concepts.definition: The self becomes strongly identified with or experientially takes on a social role, fictional character, or archetype without a specific animal or inanimate transformation.
concepts.name: role identification

concepts.definition: A habitual social persona, performance, or masking strategy falls away or becomes difficult to maintain, revealing less filtered self-presentation.
concepts.name: social mask suppression

concepts.definition: The felt authorship, intentional control, and ability to direct one's own actions become unusually strong, distinct from confidence in performing them successfully.
concepts.name: agency enhancement

concepts.definition: The person feels fraudulent, undeserving, or illegitimate in a role or identity despite external evidence of belonging or competence.
concepts.name: impostor feeling

concepts.definition: A broad fallback for a directly felt sacred, transcendent, existential, or noetic alteration when the report does not establish a narrower phenomenological structure.
concepts.name: spiritual experience

concepts.definition: A person, place, event, or experience is felt to possess holy, inviolable, reverential, or numinous quality, independently of formal religious belief.
concepts.name: sacredness

concepts.definition: Knowledge or understanding feels received, unveiled, or disclosed as a revelation rather than reached through ordinary inference; its topic belongs in detail.
concepts.name: revelatory insight

concepts.definition: A new understanding concerns existence, mortality, freedom, purpose, identity, or the meaning of life, without necessarily feeling supernaturally revealed or certainly true.
concepts.name: existential insight

concepts.definition: An event, idea, or experience feels important at a universal, ultimate, or reality-wide scale, beyond personal salience alone.
concepts.name: cosmic significance

concepts.definition: A distinct person, being, entity, or agent is felt to be nearby despite not being ordinarily perceived, without requiring a visual or auditory hallucination.
concepts.name: sensed presence

concepts.definition: People, nature, events, or existence are felt to participate in a pervasive web of relation or mutual belonging while their individual identities may remain.
concepts.name: interconnectedness

concepts.definition: The spiritual or existential self feels newly born, renewed, purified, or begun again, rather than merely improved in mood or self-acceptance.
concepts.name: spiritual rebirth

concepts.definition: An insight or experience carries a direct felt quality of unquestionable truth or objective knowledge, even when ordinary evidence is absent.
concepts.name: noetic certainty

concepts.definition: The experience itself feels intrinsically resistant to adequate expression in words or concepts, beyond ordinary difficulty remembering or explaining it.
concepts.name: ineffability

concepts.definition: Awareness remains present without ordinary thought, image, object, self-narrative, or differentiated content; this is not confusion, sedation, or mind blanking.
concepts.name: pure awareness

concepts.definition: Apparently contradictory qualities or propositions are directly experienced as simultaneously true or reconciled within a larger unity, rather than merely producing ambivalence.
concepts.name: coincident opposites

concepts.definition: Two or more events are experienced as meaningfully connected coincidences despite no established ordinary causal link between them.
concepts.name: synchronicity perception

concepts.definition: A nonhuman object, place, plant, landscape, or process is directly felt to be alive, ensouled, minded, or intentional rather than merely moving visually.
concepts.name: animistic attribution

concepts.definition: Events feel destined, predetermined, or meant to happen as they do, distinct from simply feeling important, true, or meaningfully coincidental.
concepts.name: fatedness

concepts.definition: A broad fallback for a directly experienced alteration in social motivation, connection, understanding, or interpersonal stance when no narrower social effect is established.
concepts.name: social change

concepts.definition: Seeking and enjoying social interaction becomes easier or more desirable, beyond merely speaking more once interaction has already begun.
concepts.name: sociability enhancement

concepts.definition: The amount, frequency, or continuity of speech increases, without by itself establishing confidence, openness, sociability, stimulation, or elevated mood.
concepts.name: talkativeness

concepts.definition: The capacity or tendency to understand, resonate with, or feel another person's emotional state or experience becomes stronger.
concepts.name: empathy enhancement

concepts.definition: Willingness to engage, be receptive, share, or encounter others with reduced interpersonal guardedness increases, without requiring intimate disclosure.
concepts.name: social openness

concepts.definition: Assurance and ease in social interaction increase, with less felt uncertainty about one's ability to participate effectively or be evaluated favorably.
concepts.name: social confidence

concepts.definition: Social interaction or anticipated evaluation evokes anxiety, self-consciousness, or fear of negative judgment, beyond a preference to be alone.
concepts.name: social anxiety

concepts.definition: The desire or tendency to disengage from social contact and reduce interaction increases, whether caused by anxiety, low interest, overwhelm, or another state.
concepts.name: withdrawal

concepts.definition: Another person or group seems to accurately grasp one's inner experience, meaning, or perspective, distinct from merely agreeing or feeling generally connected.
concepts.name: feeling understood

concepts.definition: A direct sense of interpersonal closeness, bond, or relation to another person or people increases without requiring altered self-boundaries or group-wide equality.
concepts.name: feeling connected

concepts.definition: A group is experienced through unusual equality, shared humanity, and collective togetherness that temporarily transcends ordinary roles or hierarchy.
concepts.name: communitas

concepts.definition: The person feels estranged, separate, or unable to participate in the social world or with surrounding people, beyond simply choosing solitude.
concepts.name: feeling alienated

concepts.definition: Other people feel more reliable, safe, honest, or worthy of reliance than usual, independently of general openness or affection.
concepts.name: trust enhancement

concepts.definition: Other people feel less reliable, safe, honest, or worthy of reliance than usual, without requiring a specific belief that they intend harm.
concepts.name: trust suppression

concepts.definition: The capacity or willingness to understand, resonate with, or feel another person's emotional state becomes reduced, independently of broad emotional blunting.
concepts.name: empathy suppression

concepts.definition: Possible dislike, exclusion, criticism, or abandonment is detected more readily and produces disproportionate emotional concern, even from ambiguous cues.
concepts.name: rejection sensitivity

concepts.definition: Emotional closeness, mutual access, or capacity for deeply personal connection becomes stronger, beyond general sociability or feeling connected.
concepts.name: intimacy enhancement

concepts.definition: Motivation to help, protect, share with, or benefit others increases without requiring personal reward, emotional resonance, or concern about suffering.
concepts.name: altruism enhancement

concepts.definition: The person feels more accepted, included, at home, or legitimately part of a group or community, distinct from interpersonal closeness alone.
concepts.name: belongingness enhancement

concepts.definition: The felt bond, attachment need, or desire to maintain proximity to a particular person becomes stronger, beyond affection or immediate intimacy.
concepts.name: attachment enhancement

concepts.definition: A compelling desire to reveal, confess, or share personal information and inner truths arises, distinct from increased speech quantity or passive openness.
concepts.name: disclosure urge

concepts.definition: Validation, praise, permission, or favorable evaluation from others feels unusually necessary or motivating, beyond sensitivity to outright rejection.
concepts.name: approval seeking

concepts.definition: Disagreement, confrontation, or interpersonal tension becomes unusually difficult to tolerate and is more strongly avoided, even at personal cost.
concepts.name: conflict aversion

concepts.definition: An increased urge is felt to shield a person, being, group, or valued object from danger, distress, or harm.
concepts.name: protectiveness

concepts.definition: The person feels socially commanding, leading, controlling, or higher in interpersonal position, distinct from simple confidence or inflated global importance.
concepts.name: dominance feelings

concepts.definition: The person feels inclined to yield, defer, follow, or accept another's interpersonal control, beyond avoiding conflict from fear or anxiety.
concepts.name: submissiveness

concepts.definition: Attention more frequently or strongly compares one's traits, status, outcomes, or worth with those of other people.
concepts.name: social comparison enhancement

concepts.definition: Coordinating efforts, sharing goals, compromising, or working jointly with others feels easier or more motivating than usual.
concepts.name: cooperation enhancement

concepts.definition: The ability or urge to state needs, preferences, opinions, and refusals clearly and directly increases, without requiring dominance over others.
concepts.name: assertiveness enhancement

concepts.definition: The desire or ability to define and enforce interpersonal limits increases, including saying no or restricting access without broader confrontation.
concepts.name: boundary setting enhancement

concepts.definition: The urge to align attitudes, appearance, or behavior with a group increases in order to fit its norms, distinct from cooperation toward a shared task.
concepts.name: conformity enhancement

concepts.definition: An increased urge to oppose, disagree with, or take the reverse position from others occurs beyond evidence-based skepticism or defense against criticism.
concepts.name: contrarianism

concepts.definition: The ability to model another person's viewpoint, knowledge, intentions, or interpretation becomes stronger, without necessarily sharing that person's emotion.
concepts.name: perspective-taking enhancement

concepts.definition: The ability to model another person's viewpoint, knowledge, intentions, or interpretation becomes reduced, even when the person's emotion may still be sensed.
concepts.name: perspective-taking impairment

concepts.definition: The desire to win, outperform, rank above, or prevail against others becomes more salient and motivating, distinct from simply feeling dominant.
concepts.name: competitiveness

concepts.definition: The inclination to comply with instructions or authority increases, beyond yielding interpersonally or matching the behavior of a peer group.
concepts.name: obedience enhancement

concepts.definition: Concern about controlling access to personal information, space, or inner life becomes reduced, independently of an active urge to disclose.
concepts.name: privacy concern suppression

concepts.definition: Monitoring and deliberately shaping how one appears to others becomes more prominent, including curating speech, behavior, image, or emotional display.
concepts.name: impression management enhancement

concepts.definition: Concern about observation, secrecy, personal boundaries, or control of private information becomes stronger, without requiring persecutory suspicion.
concepts.name: privacy concern enhancement

concepts.definition: One's emotions, intentions, or inner condition feel plainly visible and readable to others, without necessarily believing that literal thoughts are transmitted.
concepts.name: transparency feeling

concepts.definition: A broad fallback for an alteration in externally directed touch perception when no narrower change in intensity, quality, location, or recognition is established.
concepts.name: tactile change

concepts.definition: Real touch, texture, pressure, or contact feels unusually intense, detailed, vivid, or salient; its pleasantness or unpleasantness belongs in detail or a separate effect.
concepts.name: tactile amplification

concepts.definition: Real touch, texture, pressure, or contact feels unusually faint, distant, muted, or difficult to detect without being wholly numb.
concepts.name: tactile attenuation

concepts.definition: A real touch stimulus feels qualitatively unlike its physical character, such as wet, rubbery, rough, or moving when it is not.
concepts.name: tactile distortion

concepts.definition: The skin reacts to ordinary contact, clothing, air, or temperature with unusual tenderness, irritation, or sensory reactivity rather than simple intensity gain.
concepts.name: skin sensitivity

concepts.definition: A touch is felt at the wrong bodily location, over an enlarged area, or displaced from where the stimulus actually contacts the body.
concepts.name: tactile localization distortion

concepts.definition: A touched object's identity, shape, or material becomes difficult to recognize by touch despite the contact itself still being sensed.
concepts.name: tactile recognition impairment

concepts.definition: Touch, pressure, movement, contact, or another tactile event is felt without a matching external stimulus; its location and content belong in detail.
concepts.name: tactile hallucination

concepts.definition: A broad fallback for a directly experienced alteration in sexual desire, sensuality, arousal, function, or orgasm when no narrower effect is supported.
concepts.name: sexual change

concepts.definition: Sexual desire, interest, or motivation becomes stronger or more frequent, independently of current genital arousal or general tactile pleasure.
concepts.name: increased libido

concepts.definition: Sexual desire, interest, or motivation becomes weaker or absent, independently of whether physiological arousal remains possible.
concepts.name: decreased libido

concepts.definition: Sensory and embodied experiences feel more sensuous, intimate, or erotically textured without necessarily producing explicit sexual desire or genital arousal.
concepts.name: increased sensuality

concepts.definition: Subjective or physiological sexual arousal arises more readily or intensely, distinct from the motivational desire measured by libido.
concepts.name: sexual arousal enhancement

concepts.definition: Subjective or physiological sexual arousal is reduced or difficult to sustain despite context or desire that would ordinarily support it.
concepts.name: sexual arousal suppression

concepts.definition: A broad functional difficulty affects sexual response or activity but the report does not establish a narrower arousal or orgasm-related impairment.
concepts.name: sexual dysfunction

concepts.definition: Orgasm is experienced as unusually intense, prolonged, full-bodied, or subjectively satisfying once it occurs.
concepts.name: orgasm enhancement

concepts.definition: Reaching orgasm takes unusually long or requires substantially more stimulation, while orgasm remains possible.
concepts.name: orgasm delay

concepts.definition: Orgasm cannot be reached despite sexual stimulation or arousal that would ordinarily be sufficient, rather than merely being delayed.
concepts.name: anorgasmia

concepts.definition: An orgasm occurs without deliberate sexual stimulation or an ordinary triggering activity; its context and bodily focus belong in detail.
concepts.name: spontaneous orgasm

concepts.definition: A broad fallback for a directly experienced change in sleep, dreaming, or sleep-wake transition when no narrower phenomenon is established.
concepts.name: sleep disturbance

concepts.definition: Adequate sleep is persistently or substantially unavailable despite an opportunity to sleep, potentially involving onset, maintenance, or early awakening.
concepts.name: insomnia

concepts.definition: Transitioning from wakefulness into sleep takes unusually long or feels repeatedly interrupted, without necessarily implying broader insomnia across the night.
concepts.name: difficulty falling asleep

concepts.definition: Sleep is repeatedly broken by awakenings or brief returns to wakefulness, preventing a continuous sleep period despite successful sleep onset.
concepts.name: sleep fragmentation

concepts.definition: Dreams contain unusually intense, detailed, lifelike, colorful, or emotionally immediate experience without requiring awareness that one is dreaming.
concepts.name: vivid dreams

concepts.definition: Awareness that one is currently dreaming occurs within the dream, whether or not the dream's events can be deliberately controlled.
concepts.name: lucid dreams

concepts.definition: Dream content is remembered after waking with greater frequency, duration, or detail than is usual for the reporter.
concepts.name: dream recall enhancement

concepts.definition: Wakefulness becomes difficult to maintain and sleep onset feels imminent, distinct from low energy without a direct tendency to fall asleep.
concepts.name: drowsiness

concepts.definition: Image-like, auditory, tactile, or other dreamlike experiences arise during the transition from wakefulness into sleep while some awareness is retained.
concepts.name: hypnagogia

concepts.definition: Image-like, auditory, tactile, or other dreamlike experiences persist or arise during the transition from sleep into wakefulness.
concepts.name: hypnopompia

concepts.definition: Awareness returns at sleep onset or awakening while voluntary skeletal movement remains temporarily unavailable, sometimes alongside transitional imagery.
concepts.name: sleep paralysis

concepts.definition: The person dreams that they have awakened and begun ordinary waking activity, only later recognizing that the apparent awakening occurred within a dream.
concepts.name: false awakening

concepts.definition: Dream events or memories are difficult to distinguish from waking events after or around sleep, rather than simply feeling that waking life is dreamlike.
concepts.name: dream-reality confusion

concepts.definition: Dreams are intensely distressing, threatening, or frightening and commonly provoke awakening or lingering distress, beyond vividness alone.
concepts.name: nightmares

concepts.definition: Sleep duration or the need to sleep becomes substantially greater than usual, beyond a brief episode of drowsiness or ordinary recovery sleep.
concepts.name: hypersomnia
